text: 建禮門院は、東山の麓、吉田の邊なる所にぞ、立入せ給ひける。中納言法印慶惠と申ける奈良法師の坊なりけり。住荒して年久しう成ければ庭には草深く、軒にはしのぶ茂れり。簾たえ閨露はにて、雨風たまるべうもなし。花は色々匂へども主と憑む人もなく、月は夜な／＼さし入れども、詠めて明す主もなし。昔は玉の臺を磨き、錦の帳に纒れて、明し暮し給ひしが、今は有とし有人には、皆別果てて、あさましげなる朽坊に入らせ給ひける御心の中おしはかられて哀なり。魚の陸に上れるが如く、鳥の巣を離たるが如し。さるまゝには、憂りし波の上、船の中の御住ひも、今は戀しうぞ思召す。蒼波路遠し、思を西海千里の雲に寄せ、白屋苔深くして、涙東山一庭の月に落つ。悲しとも云ばかりなし。

annotation.translation: The retired Empress Kenreimon entered the place at the foot of Higashiyama, near Yoshida. It was the monastery of the Nara monk known as the Chūnagon Hōin Kekei. Having lived there in desolation for many years, the garden was overgrown with deep grass, and the eaves were thick with creeping vines. The blinds were broken, and the dew of the sleeping chamber was undisturbed; there was no place to shelter from rain or wind. Though flowers of various kinds emitted their scents, there was no one to rely upon as a host; though the moon shone in night after night, there was no host to compose poems and greet the dawn. In former days, she polished the jade platform and was wrapped in brocade curtains, living from morning to evening, but now, to those who are worthy and those who are not, all has come to an end, and her heart, which entered the pitifully dilapidated monastery, is perceived and is sorrowful. It is like a fish washed up on land, like a bird that has left its nest. Under such circumstances, she now longs to dwell in the boat upon the troubled waves. The path of blue waves is far; she sends her thoughts to the clouds of the Western Sea a thousand ri away, while her white house is covered in deep moss, and her tears fall upon the moon in the single courtyard of Higashiyama. There is nothing but sorrow to be spoken.

text: かくて女院は文治元年五月一日、御ぐし下させ給けり。御戒の師には、長樂寺の阿證房の上人印誓とぞ聞えし。御布施には、先帝の御直衣なり。今はの時まで召されたりければ、其移り香もいまだうせず。御形見に御覽ぜんとて、西國より遙々と都迄持せ給ひたりければ、如何ならん世までも、御身をはなたじとこそ思召されけれども、御布施になりぬべき物のなき上、且は彼御菩提の爲とて、泣々取出され給ひけり。上人是を給て、何と奏する旨もなくして、墨染の袖を絞りつつ泣々罷出でられけり。此御衣をば幡に縫て、長樂寺の佛前に懸られけるとぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: Thus, on the first day of the fifth month of the first year of Bunji, the retired Empress passed away. It was heard that the master of her precepts was Shōshōbō no Shōin of Chōraku-ji Temple. Her offering was the direct robe of the late emperor. Since she had been summoned until that time, her lingering scent remained. Because she had brought it all the way from the western provinces to the capital, intending to view it as a keepsake, she had thought that even in the coming generations she would not part with her body, but since there was no other object suitable to become an offering, and furthermore, for the sake of his spiritual repose, she tearfully took it out. The monk, receiving this, without making any report, wrung out the sumi-dyed sleeve and tearfully departed. It was heard that this robe was sewn into a banner and hung before the Buddha at Chōraku-ji Temple.

text: 女院は十五にて女御の宣旨を下され、十六にて后妃の位にそなはり、君王の側に候はせ給ひて、朝には朝政を勸め、夜は夜を專にし給へり。二十二にて皇子御誕生有て、皇太子に立ち、位につかせ給しかば、院號蒙らせ給ひて、建禮門院とぞ申ける。入道相國の御娘なる上、天子の國母にてましましければ世の重し奉る事斜ならず。今年は二十九にぞならせ給ふ。桃李の御粧猶濃かに、芙蓉の御容未だ衰させ給はねども、翡翠の御かざしつけても何にかはせさせ給ふべきなれば、遂に御樣をかへさせ給ひ、浮世を厭ひ、實の道に入せ給へども、御歎きは更に盡せず。人人今はかくとて海に沈し有樣、先帝、二位殿の御面影、如何ならん世までも忘がたく思食すに露の御命何しに今までながらへて、かゝる憂目を見るらんと思食めし續けて御涙せきあへさせ給はず。五月の短夜なれども明しかねさせ給ひつゝ、自打睡ませ給はねば、昔の事は夢にだにも御覽ぜず。壁に背ける殘の燈の影幽に、夜もすがら窓打暗き雨の音ぞさびしかりける。上陽人が上陽宮に閉られけん悲みも、是には過じとぞ見えし。昔を忍ぶ妻となれとてや、本の主の移し栽たりけん花橘の軒近く風なつかしう香りけるに、山郭公二聲三聲音信ければ、女院ふるき事なれ共、思召出でて、御硯の蓋にかうぞ遊ばされける。

annotation.translation: The Empress Dowager, at the age of fifteen, was granted the title of Nyogo; at sixteen, she ascended to the rank of Kōhi, and was allowed to attend the Emperor, advising him on morning governance and dedicating herself to night duties. At twenty-two, she gave birth to a Prince, who was established as Crown Prince, and upon being installed as Emperor, she received the title of In and was called the Kenreimon-in. As the daughter of the Retired Prime Minister and the Mother of the Emperor, she was held in great esteem by the world. This year, she turns twenty-nine. Her peach and plum-like beauty remains vivid, and her lotus-like countenance has not yet begun to fade, yet even with the finest jade ornaments, she could not help but feel that her appearance could not be maintained; thus, she finally changed her appearance, grew weary of the floating world, and entered the path of the True Way, yet her sighs were far from exhausted. Seeing how everyone now sinks into the sea of sorrow, she thought with great difficulty how the former Emperor and the Second Rank Lady might be forgotten even in the world to come, and wondered how long her dew-like life would continue to witness such sorrowful scenes, but she could not restrain her tears from falling. Although it was a short summer night, she could not sleep, and since she did not drift into a light doze, she did not even see the past in dreams. The shadow of the remaining lamp leaning against the wall was dim, and the sound of the dark rain beating against the window all night was indeed desolate. Even the sorrow of the Upper Yang Lady confined in the Upper Yang Palace did not surpass this. Thinking of herself as a wife who remembered the past, she pondered whether the flower of the hawthorn, transplanted near the eaves of the original master's house, had grown so dear to the wind that it smelled nostalgically; when the Mountain Crow's two and three calls could no longer be heard, the Empress Dowager, though it was an old matter, brought forth her thoughts and played with the lid of the inkstone in this manner.

text: 女房達は、さのみたけく、二位殿、越前の三位の上の樣に、水の底にも沈み給ねば、武士の荒けなきにとらはれて、舊里に歸り、若きも老たるも樣をかへ、形をやつし、在にもあられぬ有樣にてぞ、思ひもかけぬ谷の底、岩の挾間に明し暮し給ひける。住し宿は皆烟と上りにしかば、空しき跡のみ殘りて、茂き野邊と成つゝ、見馴し人の問くるもなし。仙家より歸て、七世の孫に逢けんも、かくやと覺えて哀也。

annotation.translation: The ladies, not being as valiant as the Lady of the Second Rank or the Lady of the Third Rank of Echizen, were not able to sink into the depths of the water; they were captured by the rough warriors, returned to their old home, and whether young or old, they changed their appearance, disfigured their forms, and lived in such a wretched state that they were not even recognizable, spending their days and nights in the deep valley bottom and among the narrow rock crevices. As their dwellings all rose up as smoke, only empty traces remained, becoming overgrown fields, and even familiar people came to inquire but found none. Returning from the immortals, even if one were to meet one's seventh-generation grandchild, one would think, 'Is this so?' and feel deep sorrow.

text: さる程に七月九日の大地震に、築地も壞れ、荒たる御所も傾き破れて、いとゞ住せ給べき御便もなし、緑衣の監使宮門を守だにもなし。心の儘に荒たる籬は、茂き野邊よりも露けく、折知がほに、何しか蟲の聲々恨るも哀也。夜も漸々長く成れば、いとゞ御寢覺がちにて、明しかねさせ給ひけり。盡せぬ御物思ひに、秋の哀さへうち添て、しのびがたくぞ思食されける。何事も變り果ぬるうきよなれば、自なさけを懸奉るべき草のゆかりも枯果てて、誰はぐくみ奉るべしとも見え給はず。

annotation.translation: In this manner, during the great earthquake of the ninth day of the seventh month, the moat collapsed, and the ruined palace tilted and fell apart; there was not even a convenient place for the Emperor to reside. Even the imperial guards in green robes did not guard the palace gates. The thicket, abandoned as it was, was more exposed than the lush wilds, and in its broken and withered state, even the lamentable cries of the insects were sorrowful. As the nights gradually grew longer, the Emperor found it increasingly difficult to sleep and could not rise in the morning. Overwhelmed by his unquenchable thoughts of the past, the sadness of autumn seemed to intensify, and he felt he could no longer endure it. For this world had become utterly changed and wretched, even the humble ties of grass that might have offered him pity had withered and perished, and no one appeared who could show him compassion.

text: されども冷泉大納言隆房卿の北方、七條修理大夫信隆卿の北方しのびつゝやう／＼に訪ひ申させ給ひけり。「あの人共のはぐくみで有るべしとこそ昔は思はざりしか。」とて女院御涙を流させ給へば、附參せたる女房達も、皆袖をぞ絞られける。

annotation.translation: Nevertheless, the Northern Lady of the Cold-Stream Dainagon Takafusa no Mikoto, and the Northern Lady of the Shichijō Shūji Tadanori no Mikoto, came to visit them secretly and in various ways. "They must have been raised by those people," she thought, "for in the past I had not thought so." And when the Empress Dowager was moved to shed tears, all the ladies-in-waiting who attended her also wrung their sleeves.

text: 此御すまひも猶都近く、玉鉾の道行人の人目も繁くて、露の御命の風を待ん程は、憂事きかぬ深き山の奧へも入なばやとはおぼしけれども、さるべき便もましまさず。或女房の參て申けるは、「大原山の奧寂光院と申處こそ、靜かに候へ。」と申ければ。「山里は、物のさびしき事こそあるなれども、世の憂よりは住よかんなるものを。」とて、思食し立せ給ひけり。御輿などは隆房卿の北方の御沙汰有けるとかや。文治元年長月の末に、かの寂光院へ入らせ給ふ。道すがら四方の梢の色々なるを、御覽じ過させ給ふ程に、山陰なればにや、日も既に暮かゝりぬ。野寺の鐘の入相の音すごく、分る草葉の露滋み、いとど御袖濕勝、嵐烈く木の葉亂りがはし。空かき曇り、いつしか打時雨つゝ、鹿の音幽に音信て、蟲の恨も絶々なり。とにかくに取集たる御心細さ、譬へ遣べき方もなし。浦傳ひ島傳ひせし時も、さすがかくは無かりしものをと思召こそ悲けれ。岩に苔むして、寂たる處なりければ、住まほしうぞ思しめす。露結ぶ庭の萩原霜枯れて、籬の菊のかれ／＼に、移ろふ色を御覽じても、御身の上とや覺しけん。

annotation.translation: This residence too is still near the capital; the road of the jade halberd is thronged with many people, and though one might think it would be better to enter even into the deep recesses of a mountain where one hears no sorrowful news while awaiting the wind of the dew-like life, there is no such convenient means. A certain lady came and said, 'It is at the deep recesses of Ohara Mountain, the Jigokudani Temple, where one may dwell quietly.' When she said this, she thought, 'Though the mountain village may have things that are desolate, it is better to live there than to endure the sorrows of the world,' and she resolved to go. As for the palanquin and the like, it is said that the Northern Lady of Prince Takafusa made arrangements. In the late month of the eighth month of the first year of Bunji, she was allowed to enter that Jigokudani Temple. As she gazed upon the various treetops in all directions along the way, since it was in the shadow of the mountains, perhaps the day had already grown late. The sound of the bell of the mountain temple at the time of the gathering was loud; the dew on the distinguishable grass leaves became wet, and her sleeves grew even more damp, while the wind blew fiercely and the leaves of the trees began to scatter. The sky grew dark and cloudy, and soon it began to rain in showers; the sound of deer was faint and the insects' lament seemed to cease entirely. There was no way to compare the great anxiety that had been gathered up. 'Even when I traveled from bay to bay, I was not in such a state,' she thought, and she felt sorrowful. Since it was a place covered with moss and desolate, she thought she would like to live there. In the garden where dew formed, the bush clover of the frost-dried field withered; the chrysanthemums of the hedge were withered in various ways; even as she gazed upon their changing colors, she wondered whether she perceived it as her own body.

text: 佛の御前へ參せ給ひて、「天子聖靈、成等正覺、頓證菩提。」と祈り申させ給ふにつけても先帝の御面影、ひしと御身に傍ひて、如何ならん世にか思召忘れさせ給ふべき。さて寂光院の傍に、方丈なる御庵室を結んで、一間をば御寢所に定め、一間をば佛所に定め、晝夜朝夕の御勤、長時不斷の御念佛、怠る事なくて月日を送らせ給ひけり。

annotation.translation: When he went to pay his respects before the Buddha and prayed, saying, 'May the sacred spirit of the Emperor attain perfect enlightenment and immediately realize Buddhahood,' the visage of the late Emperor appeared so vividly beside him that how could he possibly forget his thoughts of the world to come? Thus, beside Jikō-in, he constructed a small hut of one square, designating one room as his sleeping quarters and the other as a place of worship. Day and night, morning and evening, he diligently performed his devotions, reciting the nembutsu without interruption day after day.

text: 女院哀に思食し、窓の小障子に此歌を遊ばし留させ給ひけり。

annotation.translation: The Lady Empress felt sorrow and had this poem written on the small lattice window.

text: かゝる御つれ％＼の中に、思しめしなぞらふる事どもは、つらき中にも餘たあり。軒に竝べる樹をば、七重寶樹とかたどれり。岩間に積る水をば、八功徳水と思食す。無常は春の花、風に隨てちりやすく、有涯は秋の月、雲に伴て隱易し。昭陽殿に花を翫びし朝には、風來て匂を散し、長秋宮に月を詠ぜし夕には、雲掩て光を藏す。昔は玉樓金殿に錦の褥をしき、妙なりし御すまひなりしかども、今は柴引結ぶ草の庵、餘所の袂もしをれけり。

annotation.translation: Among such misfortunes, there are matters to be considered as the Lord's will. The trees lined up on the eaves are likened to the seven-tiered jewel trees. The water accumulated in the rock crevices is thought of as the water of the eight virtues. Impermanence is like the spring flowers, easily scattered by the wind; finitude is like the autumn moon, easily hidden by the clouds. On the morning when the flowers were enjoyed in the Shoyo Hall, the wind came and scattered their fragrance; on the evening when the moon was chanted in the Chōkyū Palace, the clouds covered and hid its light. text: かゝりし程に、文治二年の春の比、法皇建禮門院大原の閑居の御住ひ御覽ぜまほしう思食されけれども、きさらぎ彌生の程は、嵐烈く餘寒も未だ盡せず。嶺の白雪消やらで、谷のつららも打解ず。春過ぎ夏來て、北祭も過しかば、法皇夜を籠めて、大原の奧へぞ御幸なる。忍びの御幸なりけれども、供奉の人々は、徳大寺、花山院、土御門以下、公卿六人、殿上人八人、北面少々候ひけり。鞍馬どほりの御幸なれば、彼清原深養父が補陀洛寺、小野の皇太后宮の舊跡を叡覽有て、其より御輿に召されけり。遠山に懸る白雲は、散にし花の形見なり。青葉に見ゆる梢には、春の名殘ぞをしまるゝ。比は卯月廿日餘の事なれば、夏草の茂みが末を分入せ給に、始めたる御幸なれば、御覽じ馴たる方もなく、人跡絶たる程も思召しられて哀なり。

annotation.translation: As things had come to pass, in the spring of the second year of Bunji, the Emperor wished to visit the retired Emperor's retirement residence at Ohara, but during the months of Kisaragi and Yayoi, the winds were fierce and the lingering cold had not yet subsided. The white snow on the peaks had not melted, and the icicles in the valleys had not yet broken. After spring passed and summer came, and the Northern Festival had also passed, the retired Emperor stayed up all night and then proceeded to the depths of Ohara. Though it was a secret visit, the attendants included six court nobles—Daidaiji, Hanazan-in, Tsuchimikado, and others below—and eight palace attendants, along with a few men of the Northern Guard. Since the excursion was to Mount Kurama, the retired Emperor first viewed with his enlightened eyes the former site of Jodoji Temple of Kiyohara no Fukayasu and the old grounds of the Empress Dowager Ono, and from there was carried in a palanquin. The white clouds hanging over the distant mountains are the tokens of the scattered flowers. In the green leaves, the treetops show the lingering traces of spring. Since this was a matter of the twentieth day or so of the fourth month, the thick summer grass was so lush that it parted the path. Because it was the first such excursion, there were no ones accustomed to viewing such sights, and the thought that the place was utterly devoid of human footprints was deemed sad.

text: 西の山の麓に、一宇の御堂有り、即寂光院是なり。古う作りなせる山水木立、由ある樣の所なり。「甍破れては霧不斷の香を燒き、とぼそ落ては月常住の燈を挑ぐ。」とも、か樣の處をや申すべき。庭の夏草茂り合ひ、青柳糸を亂りつゝ、池の浮草浪に漂ひ、錦をさらすかとあやまたる。中島の松に懸れる藤波の、うら紫に咲る色、青葉交りの晩櫻、初花よりも珍しく、岸の山吹咲き亂れ、八重立雲の絶間より、山郭公の一聲も、君の御幸を待がほなり。法皇是を叡覽有て、かうぞ思召しつゞけける。

annotation.translation: At the foot of the western mountain stands a single hall, namely the Shikō-in. Its anciently constructed landscape, with mountains, water, trees, and groves, is a place of great significance. "When the roof tiles break, the mist burns with an unceasing fragrance; when they fall scantily, the lamp of eternal moon is lit." One might say it is such a place. The summer grass in the garden grows thick and lush, the threads of the green willow become disordered, the floating plants on the pond drift with the waves, leading one to mistake them for spreading brocade. The wisteria cascading from the pines on the central island blooms in a deep purple hue, the evening cherry blossoms mingling with green leaves, rarer than the first flowers; the bush clover on the shore blooms in disorder, and from the gaps in the layered clouds resembling standing clouds, even a single call of the mountain cuckoo seems to await the Emperor's visit. The Emperor, having gazed upon this with his wise eyes, continued to think thus.

text: ふりにける岩の斷間より、落くる水の音さへ、ゆゑび由ある處なり。緑蘿の垣、翠黛の山、繪にかくとも筆も及びがたし。女院の御庵室を御覽ずれば、軒には蔦槿はひかゝり、しのぶ交りの萱草、瓢箪屡空し、草顏淵之巷にしげし、藜でう深鎖せり、雨原憲之樞をうるほすとも謂つべし。杉の葺目もまばらにて、時雨も霜も置く露も、漏る月影に爭ひて、たまるべしとも見えざりけり。後は山、前は野邊、いさゝをざゝに風噪ぎ、世にたえぬ身の習ひとて、うきふし繁き竹柱、都の方の言傳は、間遠に結るませ垣や、僅に事問ふ物とては、嶺に木傳ふ猿の聲、賤士がつま木の斧の音、是等が音信ならでは、正木の葛青葛、來人稀なる所なり。

annotation.translation: From the crevice of the rock that lies spread out, even the sound of the falling water is a place of cause and meaning. The green ivy fence and the emerald-green mountains are such that even if painted, the brush could not reach them. If one were to view the Lady-in-Waiting's hermitage, wisteria and hibiscus hang from the eaves; the iris of remembrance intertwines, the gourd is often empty, and the grass resembles the alley of Yan Yuan, with a thicket of wild leeks deepening the lock. Even if the rain of the original plain were to moisten the lintel of the hermitage of Yuan Xian, one might say so. The cedar thatch is sparse; the autumn rain, the frost, and the dew left behind all vie with the leaking moonlight, and it does not seem possible for them to accumulate. Behind are the mountains, before are the fields; the wind makes a slight noise. As befits the habit of a body that does not cease in this world, the bamboo posts of the floating, heavy house—according to the traditions of the capital, is the fence tied far away, or merely a thing to ask about? The voice of the monkey passing through the ridge, and the sound of the commoner's axe on the tree stump—aside from these sounds and signs, it is a place where the people of the wild, the green and blue vines, and the travelers are rare.

text: 法皇「人や在る。」と召されけれども、御いらへ申者もなし。遙に有て、老衰へたる尼一人參りたり。「女院はいづくへ御幸成ぬるぞ。」と仰ければ、「此上の山へ花摘に入せ給ひて候。」と申。「左樣の事に仕へ奉るべき人も無きにや。さこそ世を捨る御身といひながら、御痛しうこそ。」と仰ければ、此尼申けるは、「五戒十善の御果報盡させ給ふに依て、今かゝる御目を御覽ずるにこそ候へ。捨身の行に、なじかは御身を惜ませ給ふべき。因果經には『欲知過去因、見其現在果、欲知未來果、見其現在因。』と説かれたり。過去未來の因果を、悟らせ給ひなば、つや／＼御歎あるべからず。悉達太子は十九にて、伽耶城を出で、檀特山の麓にて、木葉を連ねては肌をかくし、嶺に上て薪を採り、谷に下て水を結ぶ。難行苦行の功に依て、遂に成等正覺し給ひき。」とぞ申ける。此尼の有樣を御覽ずれば、絹布のわきも見えぬ物を結び集めてぞ著たりける。「あの有樣にても、か樣の事申す不思議さよ。」と思食して「抑汝は如何なる者ぞ。」と仰ければ、さめ／＼と泣いて、暫しは御返事にも及ばず。稍有て、涙を押て、申けるは、「申に付けても憚おぼえ候へ共、故少納言入道信西が娘、阿波の内侍と申し者にて候ふなり。母は紀伊の二位、さしも御いとほしみ深うこそ候ひしに、御覽じ忘させ給ふにつけて身の衰へぬる程も思ひしられて今更せんかたなうこそおぼえ候へ。」とて袖を顏に押當て、忍びあへぬ樣、目もあてられず。法皇も「されば汝は阿波内侍にこそあんなれ。今更御覽じ忘れける、唯夢とのみこそ思食せ。」とて御涙せきあへさせ給はず。供奉の公卿殿上人も、「不思議の尼哉と思ひたれば、理にて有けるぞ。」とぞ各申あはれける。

annotation.translation: The Emperor, saying, 'There is a person,' summoned her, but there was no one to answer. From afar, an old nun approached. 'Where has the Lady-in-Waiting gone?' he asked. 'She has gone to pick flowers in the mountains beyond,' she replied. 'Is there no one to serve in such a way? Yet you, who are said to have renounced the world, you say it is painful.' She answered, 'Because you have completed the retribution of the Five Precepts and the Ten Virtues, you now look upon this sight with such eyes. In the practice of self-sacrifice, how could you cherish your own body? The Sutra of Cause and Effect states: "If you wish to know the causes of the past, observe their effects in the present; if you wish to know the effects of the future, observe their causes in the present." If you could realize the cause and effect of the past and future, there would be no need to sigh at all. Prince Siddhartha, at the age of nineteen, left Gaya City. At the foot of Mount Dandaka, he wove tree leaves to cover his skin, climbed the mountain to gather firewood, and descended into the valley to fetch water. Through the merit of these difficult and arduous practices, he ultimately attained perfect enlightenment.' Thus she spoke. When the Emperor saw her appearance, he was wearing a robe made of torn silk fragments gathered together. 'Even with such an appearance, she speaks of such things; how strange,' he thought, and asked, 'Who are you?' She wept bitterly and, for a while, could not even respond. After a moment, wiping away her tears, she said, 'Although I am ashamed to speak, I am the daughter of the late Minor Secretary and Priest Shōnō, named Awa no Naishi. My mother was the Lady-in-Waiting of Ki, who was held in such deep affection that I thought of her even as my body aged, and now I feel I cannot bear to be forgotten by you.' With this, she pressed her sleeve to her face, unable to hold back her tears, unable to look up. The Emperor, too, said, 'So you are Awa no Naishi. Now that you have been forgotten, I shall only think of it as a dream,' and he could not hold back his tears. The accompanying nobles and high-ranking officials also thought, 'This is indeed a mysterious nun,' and each lamented, 'It is only natural.'"

text: さる程に上の山より、濃墨染の衣著たる尼二人、岩のかけぢを傳ひつゝ、おり煩ひ給ひけり。法皇是を御覽じて「あれは何ものぞ。」と御尋あれば、老尼涙を押へて、申けるは「花がたみ肱にかけ、岩躑躅取具して持せ給ひたるは、女院にて渡らせ給ひ候也。爪木に蕨折具して候ふは、鳥飼中納言維實の娘、五條大納言國綱の養子、先帝の御乳人、大納言佐。」と申もあへず泣けり。法皇も世に哀氣に思食して御涙せきあへさせ給はず。女院は「さこそ世を捨つる御身といひながら今かゝる御有樣を見え參せんずらん慚しさよ、消も失ばや。」と思しめせどもかひぞなき。宵々毎の閼伽の水、むすぶ袂もしをるるに、曉起の袖の上、山路の露も滋して、絞りやかねさせ給ひけん、山へも歸らせ給はず、御庵室へも入せ給はず、御涙に咽ばせ給ひ、あきれて立せまし／＼たるところに、内侍の尼參りつゝ、花がたみをば給はりけり。

annotation.translation: In this manner, two nuns dressed in heavy indigo-dyed robes descended from the upper mountain, moving from rock to rock with difficulty. The retired emperor, upon seeing this, inquired, "What are they?" The elderly nun, holding back her tears, replied, "The one draped in a floral-patterned garment and carrying a rhododendron branch is the Lady-in-Waiting [Nyoin] who sent her forth. The one plucking ferns and holding them is the daughter of the Middle Counselor Torikai, adopted son of the Senior Counselor Kounetsu, and former wet nurse of the late emperor, Senior Counselor Sata." She could not finish speaking before breaking down in tears. The retired emperor, filled with sorrow for the world, could not hold back his tears. Though the Lady-in-Waiting thought, "Even though one says one has renounced the world, to now appear in such a state is truly shameful; I wish I could vanish from sight," her thoughts were in vain. Night after night, the water of the offering bowl [agama] has soaked her sleeves, and the dew of the mountain path on the upper part of her morning sleeves has become so wet that she cannot wring them dry. She has not returned to the mountain, nor has she entered her hermitage. Choking with tears, she stood, bewildered and wandering. Then, a nun of the Chamberlain came forward and presented her with the floral-patterned garment.

「世を厭ふ習ひ、何かは苦しう候ふべき。疾疾御對面候うて還御なし參らさせ給へ。」と申ければ、女院御庵室に入らせ給ふ。「一念の窓の前には、攝取の光明を期し、十念の柴のとぼそには、聖衆の來迎をこそ待つるに、思の外に御幸なりける不思議さよ。」とて、御見參有けり。法皇此御有樣を見參らせ給て「悲想之八萬劫、猶必滅の愁に逢ひ、欲界の六天、未だ五衰の悲をまぬかれず。善見城の勝妙の樂、中間禪の高臺の閣、又夢の裏の果報幻の間の樂、既に流轉無窮也。車輪の廻るが如し。天人の五衰の悲みは人間にも候ひける物かな。」とぞ仰ける。「さるにても、誰か事問ひ參せ候。何事に附ても、さこそ古思しめし出候らめ。」と仰ければ「何方よりも音信る事も候はず。隆房、信隆の北の方より、絶々申送る事こそさぶらへ。その昔、あの人どものはぐくみにて有るべしとは、露も思ひ寄候はず。」とて、御涙を流させ給へば、附參せたる女房たちも、袖をぞぬらされける。女院御涙を押て申させ給ひけるは、「かかる身になる事は、一旦の歎き申すに及び候はねども、後生菩提の爲には、悦とおぼえさぶらふ也。忽に釋迦の遺弟に列なり、忝なく彌陀の本願に乘じて、五障三從の苦みを遁れ、三時に六根をきよめ、一筋に九品の淨刹を願ふ。專一門の菩提を祈り、常は三尊の來迎を期す。何の世にも忘がたきは先帝の御面影、忘れんとすれどもわすられず、しのばんとすれどもしのばれず。唯恩愛の道程、悲かりける事はなし。されば彼菩提の爲に、朝夕の勤め怠る事候はず。是も然べき善知識とこそ覺え候へ。」と申させ給ひければ、法皇仰せなりけるは、「此國は粟散邊土なりといへども、忝くも十善の餘薫に答へて萬乘の主となり、隨分一として心にかなはずといふ事なし。就中佛法流布の世に生て佛道修行の志あれば、後生善處疑あるべからず。人間のあだなる習は今更驚くべきにはあらねど、御有樣見奉るに、餘に爲方なうこそ候へ。」と仰ければ、女院重て申させ給ひけるは、「我平相國の娘として、天子の國母となりしかば、一天四海皆掌のまゝなりき。拜禮の春の始より、色々の衣がへ、佛名の年の暮、攝禄以下の大臣公卿にもてなされし有樣、六欲四禪の雲の上にて、八萬の諸天に圍繞せられ候ふらむ樣に、百官悉く仰ぬ者や候ひし。清凉紫宸の床の上、玉の簾の中にて持成され、春は南殿の櫻に心をとめて日を暮し、九夏三伏のあつき日は、泉をむすびて心を慰み、秋は雲の上の月を獨見ん事許されず、玄冬素雪の寒き夜は、つまを重ねて暖にす。長生不老の術を願ひ、蓬莱不死の藥を尋ねても、唯久しからん事をのみ思へり。明ても、暮れても、樂しみ榮えし事、天上の果報も、是には過じとこそ覺え候ひしか。それに壽永の秋の初、木曾義仲とかやに恐れて、一門の人々住馴し都をば雲井の餘所に顧みて、故郷を燒野の原と打詠め、古は名のみ聞し須磨より明石の浦傳ひ、さすが哀れに覺えて、晝は漫々たる浪路を分て袖をぬらし、夜は洲崎の千鳥と共に泣明し、浦々島々由ある所を見しかども、故郷の事はわすられず。かくて寄る方無りしは、五衰必滅の悲とこそおぼえ候しか。人間の事は、愛別離苦、怨憎會苦、共に、吾身に知られて候ふ。四苦八苦一として殘る所候はず。さても筑前國太宰府と云處にて、維義とかやに九國の内をも追出され、山野廣といへども立寄休むべき處なし。同じ秋の末にもなりしかば、昔は九重の雲の上にて見し月を、今は八重の鹽路に詠めつゝ、明し暮し候ひし程に、神無月の比ほひ、清經の中將が、都のうちをば源氏が爲に責落され、鎭西をば維義が爲に追出さる。網にかゝれる魚の如く、何くへ行かば遁るべきかは。存へ果べき身にもあらずとて、海に沈み候ひしぞ心憂き事の始めにて候ひし。波の上にて日を暮し、船の中にて夜を明し、御つぎ物もなかりしかば、供御を具ふる人もなし。適供御は備へんとすれども水なければ參らず。大海に浮ぶといへども、潮なれば呑事もなし。是又餓鬼道の苦とこそおぼえ候ひしか。かくて室山水島所々の戰ひに勝しかば、人々、少色なほて見え候ひし程に一谷といふ處にて一門多く滅びし後は直衣束帶を引替て、鐵をのべて身に纒ひ、明ても暮ても、軍よばひの聲斷ざりし事修羅の鬪諍、帝釋の爭ひも、かくやとこそおぼえ候ひしか。一谷を攻落されて後、親は子におくれ、妻は夫に別れ、沖に釣する船をば、敵の船かと肝を消し、遠き松に、群居鷺をば、源氏の旗かと心を盡す。さても門司赤間の關にて軍は今日を限と見えしかば、二位の尼申おく事候ひき。『男の生殘らん事は、千萬が一も有難し。縱又遠きゆかりは自生殘たりといふとも吾等が後世を弔はん事も有りがたし。昔より女は殺さぬ習ひなれば如何にもしてながらへて主上の後世をも弔ひまゐらせ、吾等が後世をも助け給へ。』と掻口説き申候ひしが、夢の心地しておぼえ候ひし程に風俄に吹き、浮雲厚くたなびいて、兵心を惑し、天運盡て、人の力に及びがたし。既に今はかうと見えしかば、二位の尼先帝を抱き奉て船端へ出し時、あきれたる御樣にて『尼ぜ我をばいづちへ具して行んとするぞ。』と仰さぶらひしに、幼き君に向ひ奉り涙を押へて申さぶらひしは、『君は未だ知し召され候はずや。先世の十善戒行の御力に依て、今萬乘の主とは生れさせ給へども、惡縁に引かれて御運既に盡給ひぬ。先づ東に向はせ給て、伊勢大神宮に御暇申させ給ひ、其後西方淨土の來迎に預らんと思食し、西に向はせ給ひて御念佛候ふべし。此國は粟散邊土とて心憂き堺にてさぶらへば、極樂淨土とて、めでたき所へ具し參せ候ふぞ。』と、泣々申候ひしかば、山鳩色の御衣に鬟結せ給ひて、御涙に溺れ、小う美くしい御手を合せ、先づ東を伏拜み、伊勢大神宮に御暇申させ給ひ、其後西に向はせ給ひて御念佛ありしかば、二位尼やがて抱き奉て海に沈みし御面影目もくれ、心も消果てて、忘んとすれ共忘られず、忍ばんとすれ共忍ばれず。殘留まる人々のをめき叫びし聲、叫喚大叫喚のほのほの底の罪人も、是れには過じとこそ覺候ひしか。さて武士共にとらはれて上り候ひし時に、播磨國明石の浦について、ちと打目睡て候ひし夢に、昔の内裏には遙に勝りたる所に、先帝を始奉て一門の公卿殿上人、皆ゆゆしげなる禮儀にて候ひしを、都を出て後、かゝる所は未だ見ざりつるに『是はいづくぞ。』と問ひ候ひしかば、二位の尼と覺えて『龍宮城』と答へ候ひし時『目出度かりける所かな。是には苦は無きか。』と問候ひしかば、『龍畜經の中に見えて候ふ、能々後世を弔ひ給へ。』と申すと覺えて夢覺ぬ。其後はいよ／＼經を讀念佛して、かの御菩提を弔奉る。是皆六道にたがはじとこそ覺え候へ。」と申させ給へば、法皇仰なりけるは、「異國の玄弉三藏は、悟りの前に六道を見、吾朝の日藏上人は、藏王權現の御力にて、六道を見たりとこそ承はれ。是程まのあたりに御覽ぜられける御事誠に有難うこそ候へ。」とて御涙に咽ばせ給へば、供奉の公卿殿上人も皆袖をぞ絞られける。女院も御涙を流させ給へば、つき參せたる女房達も又袖をぞぬらされける。

annotation.translation: "Weary of this world, I must surely suffer. Please grant me an immediate audience and return with haste." Upon hearing this, she was permitted to enter the Empress's hermitage. "Before the window of a single thought, I await the light of Amitabha's salvation; before the frail brushwood of ten recitations, I shall surely await the descent of the holy hosts. What a wonderful surprise this is!" Thus she said, and she was granted an audience. The Retired Emperor, seeing this scene, remarked, "In the eight hundred thousand kalpas of sorrow, I shall surely meet the sorrow of inevitable extinction. Even the six heavens of the Desire Realm have not yet escaped the sorrow of the Five Decays. The supreme bliss of the City of Good Vision, the lofty pavilion of the Intermediate Dhyana, and the bliss of transitory dreams and illusory retribution are all already in endless samsara, like a turning wheel. The sorrow of the Five Decays of the gods is also present for humans, is it not?" "Even so, who could ask such a question? Whatever the matter, one would surely think thus in ancient times," he replied. "No news has reached me from anywhere. Only Ryufu and Nobutaka's lady-in-waiting has sent word. In those days, I never even imagined that these people would be raised up." Thus saying, she shed tears, and the ladies-in-waiting who attended also wet their sleeves. The Empress, suppressing her tears, said, "Although it is not necessary to lament such a state of affairs for this life alone, for the sake of my future existence and enlightenment, I feel joy. I shall suddenly join the ranks of Shakyamuni's disciples, unworthily ride upon Amida's original vow, escape the sufferings of the Five Obstacles and Three Subserviences, purify the six sense organs in the three times, and single-mindedly aspire to the nine grades of the Pure Land. I pray for Bodhi with one-mindedness and always await the descent of the Three Jewels. What is most unforgettable in this world is the face of the Late Emperor; though I wish to forget him, I cannot; though I wish to suppress the memory, it cannot be suppressed. There is no sorrow in the path of affection and love. Therefore, for the sake of that Bodhi, I shall never be negligent in my morning and evening practices. I consider this to be a good teacher who is truly worthy." The Retired Emperor replied, "Although this land is but a remote land of millet seeds, I unworthily responded to the lingering fragrance of the Ten Virtues and became the sovereign of ten thousand chariots. In every respect, there is nothing that does not accord with my heart. Especially, having been born in an age where the Dharma spreads, and having the aspiration to cultivate the Buddha Way, there is no doubt of a good rebirth in the future. The nature of humans to be impermanent is no longer surprising, but seeing your state, it is truly extraordinary." The Empress replied again, "As the daughter of the Heike Chancellor and becoming the Mother of the Emperor, I held the entire world within my palm. From the beginning of spring when I paid my respects, through the changing of various robes, until the end of the year when I recited Buddha's names, the ministers and courtiers below the rank of Dainagon were all at my service. I was surrounded by eighty thousand heavenly beings as if on the clouds of the Four Dhyanas and the Six Desires. All officials bowed to me. On the bed of Seiryoden and Shishin, within the jade curtains, I was cared for. In spring, I stayed my heart on the cherry blossoms of the Southern Hall and spent the days. On the hot days of the three heats of summer, I tied springs to comfort my heart. In autumn, I was not permitted to gaze alone at the moon above the clouds. On the cold nights of the white snow of the black winter, I piled layers of clothes to keep warm. I wished for the art of life immortality and searched for the elixir of the Penglai immortals, thinking only of living long. Whether by day or by night, I felt that no joy or glory in the heavens could surpass this. Then, at the beginning of autumn in the year of Juei, fearing Kiso Yoshinaka and the like, I looked back at the capital where my clan had lived, no longer seeing it as anything but a clouded sky. I lamented my hometown as the plain of the Burning Fields. From the ancient place of Suma, where I had only heard the name, I traveled to Akashi Bay. Still, I felt great pity. By day, I divided my sleeve-wet path along the aimless waves; by night, I cried until dawn with the thousand birds of Sasaki. I visited many places, yet I could not forget my hometown. Thus, having nowhere to go, I felt the sorrow of inevitable extinction, the Five Decays. Human affairs include the suffering of separation from loved ones and the suffering of meeting those we hate. These are known to me personally. The Four Sufferings and Eight Sufferings are all present within me. Yet, at Dazaifu in Chikuzen Province, where I was driven out of the nine provinces by Minamoto no Yoritomo, though the mountains and fields were vast, there was no place to stop and rest. When the end of the same autumn came, I chanted while gazing at the moon I once saw from the nine-fold clouds of the palace, now in the eight-fold salt road, from morning to evening. Then, in the month without gods, Minamoto no Yoshitsune and the other general drove the Minamoto clan out of the capital and drove the Taira out of Chikuzen. Like fish caught in a net, where could I flee? I felt that I had no body to survive, and so I sank into the sea, the beginning of all sorrowful events. I spent days on the waves and nights in the boat. There was no provision, and no one to prepare offerings. I wished to prepare offerings, but there was no water to go and fetch. Even floating on the great sea, if the tide was high, I could not eat. I felt this was the suffering of the hungry ghost realm. Thus, after winning battles at Murasame, Shimoshima, and other places, when people looked slightly relieved, and after many of my clan perished at Ichi-no-Tani, I changed my court robes and armor, donning iron plates on my body. Whether by day or by night, the sound of military calls never ceased. I felt this was the struggle of the Asuras, the conflict of Indra. After Ichi-no-Tani was attacked and fallen, parents were left behind by children, wives separated from husbands. I mistook a boat fishing in the offing for an enemy ship, and my heart was consumed; I mistook a flock of herons on a distant pine for the Minamoto flag, and my heart was exhausted. Yet, when the army at Monji and Akama gate seemed to set today as their limit, the Lady of the Second Rank pleaded, 'It is extremely rare for a man to survive, even one in ten thousand. Even if distant relatives remain alive, it is precious for us to mourn our future. Since ancient times, women have not been killed. Please, by all means, save us so that we may also mourn the Late Emperor's future and help our own future.' She pleaded earnestly, and as if in a dream, the wind suddenly blew, thick floating clouds gathered, confused the soldiers' hearts, and the heavenly fortune ended, beyond human power. Since it was now clear that this was the case, the Lady of the Second Rank embraced the Late Emperor and carried him to the boat's edge. In a bewildered manner, he said, 'A nun! Where are you taking me?' Turning to the young prince, she suppressed her tears and replied, 'Has the Prince not yet understood? By the power of the Ten Virtues and precepts of your previous life, you were born as the sovereign of ten thousand chariots, but drawn by evil karmic connections, your fate has already ended. First, turn east, request leave from the Grand Shrine of Ise, and then, hoping to receive the descent of the Pure Land of the West, turn west and chant the Buddha's name. This land is but a remote border of millet seeds, a sorrowful place to stay. Therefore, we shall go to the blissful Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.' Thus she wept and spoke. The prince, with his hair styled in the color of mountain doves, drowned in tears, joined his small, beautiful hands, first bowed east, requested leave from the Grand Shrine of Ise, and then turned west and chanted the Buddha's name. The Lady of the Second Rank immediately embraced him and sank into the sea. His face, eyes, and heart were extinguished, yet I cannot forget him, nor can I endure the memory. The wailing and screaming of the remaining people, even the sinners at the bottom of the hot furnace of screaming and loud screaming, could not surpass this. Then, when captured by the warriors and brought ashore, arriving at Akashi Bay in Harima Province, I fell asleep for a moment and dreamed. In the dream, I saw a place far surpassing the former palace, where the Late Emperor, along with the courtiers and nobles of my clan, were all performing solemn rites. Having left the capital, I had never seen such a place before. When I asked, 'Where is this?' and the Lady of the Second Rank answered, 'The Dragon Palace,' I asked, 'What a joyous place! Is there no suffering here?' She replied, 'It appears in the Sutra of the Dragon Beasts. Please earnestly mourn our future.' Thus I awoke from the dream. Since then, I have diligently read sutras and chanted the Buddha's name to mourn that prince's soul. I consider this to be a path that will not deviate from the six realms.' Thus she spoke. The Retired Emperor replied, 'The Chinese monk Xuanzang saw the six realms before attaining enlightenment, and our own Dayzo Shonin saw the six realms through the power of the King of the Treasure. To witness such things firsthand is truly wonderful.' Thus he choked with tears, and the courtiers and nobles who attended also wrung out their sleeves. The Empress also shed tears, and the ladies-in-waiting who attended also wet their sleeves.

The prince, with his hair styled in the color of mountain doves, drowned in tears, joined his small, beautiful hands, first bowed east, requested leave from the Grand Shrine of Ise, and then turned west and chanted the Buddha's name. The Lady of the Second Rank immediately embraced him and sank into the sea. His face, eyes, and heart were extinguished, yet I cannot forget him, nor can I endure the memory. The wailing and screaming of the remaining people, even the sinners at the bottom of the hot furnace of screaming and loud screaming, could not surpass this. Then, when captured by the warriors and brought ashore, arriving at Akashi Bay in Harima Province, I fell asleep for a moment and dreamed. In the dream, I saw a place far surpassing the former palace, where the Late Emperor, along with the courtiers and nobles of my clan, were all performing solemn rites. Having left the capital, I had never seen such a place before. When I asked, 'Where is this?' and the Lady of the Second Rank answered, 'The Dragon Palace,' I asked, 'What a joyous place! Is there no suffering here?' She replied, 'It appears in the Sutra of the Dragon Beasts. Please earnestly mourn our future.' Thus I awoke from the dream. Since then, I have diligently read sutras and chanted the Buddha's name to mourn that prince's soul. I consider this to be a path that will not deviate from the six realms.' Thus she spoke. The Retired Emperor replied, 'The Chinese monk Xuanzang saw the six realms before attaining enlightenment, and our own Dayzo Shonin saw the six realms through the power of the King of the Treasure. To witness such things firsthand is truly wonderful.' Thus he choked with tears, and the courtiers and nobles who attended also wrung out their sleeves. The Empress also shed tears, and the ladies-in-waiting who attended also wet their sleeves.

text: さる程に寂光院の鐘の聲、今日も暮ぬと打しられ、夕陽西に傾けば、御名殘惜うはおぼしけれども、御涙を押て還御ならせ給ひけり。女院は今更古を思食し出させ給ひて、忍あへぬ御涙に、袖の柵塞あへさせ給はず。遙に御覽じ送らせ給ひて、還御もやう／＼延させ給ひければ、御本尊に向ひ奉り、「先帝聖靈、一門亡魂、成等正覺、頓證菩提。」と泣々祈らせ給ひけり。昔は東に向はせ給ひて「伊勢大神宮、正八幡大菩薩、天子寶算、千秋萬歳。」と申させ給ひしに、今は引かへて、西に向ひ手を合せ「過去聖靈、一佛淨土へ。」と祈らせ給ふこそ悲しけれ。御寢所の障子にかうぞ遊されける。

annotation.translation: So it was that the bell of Jikkō-in temple struck, announcing today's end as well; when the evening sun slanted westward, though she wished to linger in farewell, she restrained her tears and departed. The retired empress now began to recall the past, and with tears she could not bear, she could not keep her sleeves dry. She gazed afar and sent them off, and since her return was delayed in various ways, she turned toward her principal image and prayed, with weeping: 'May the holy spirit of the former Emperor, and the souls of the clan, attain perfect enlightenment, and suddenly realize Bodhi.' In days past she had turned east and said, 'Ise Grand Shrine, Hachiman Daibosatsu, may the Emperor's reign last a thousand autumns and ten thousand years,' but now she turned and faced west, clasping her hands and praying, 'To the holy spirits of the past, to the Pure Land of One Buddha.' This is indeed sorrowful. She had gone to her sleeping quarters and there had her screens drawn.

text: 抑壇の浦にて生ながら捕られし人々は大路を渡して頭をはねられ、妻子に離れて遠流せらる。池大納言の外は一人も命を生けられず、都に置かれず。されども四十餘人の女房達の御事は、沙汰にも[1]及ばさりしかば、親類に從ひ縁に就いてぞおはしける。上は玉の簾の中までも、風靜なる家もなく、下は柴のとぼそのもとまでも塵收れる宿もなし。枕を雙べし妹背も、雲井の餘所にぞ成果る。養ひ立し親子も、行方知らず別れけり。忍ぶ思ひは盡せねども、嘆ながらもさてこそ過されけれ。是は只入道相國、一天四海を掌に握て上は一人をも恐れず、下は萬民をも顧みず、死罪流刑、思ふ樣に行ひ、世をも人をも憚かられざりしが致す所なり。父祖の罪業は子孫に報ふと云ふ事疑なしとぞ見えたりける。

annotation.translation: Indeed, the people who were captured alive at Dan-no-ura were led across the main road, their heads severed, separated from their wives and children, and exiled to distant lands. Except for the Dainagon Ike, not a single life was spared, nor was anyone left in the capital. However, as the affairs of the forty or more court ladies did not even warrant consideration, they followed their relatives and, according to their circumstances, went into exile. Above, even within the jade curtains, there was no home without wind; below, even at the base of the brushwood piles, there was no lodging without dust. Even the sisters who shared a pillow, the 'Mise', were scattered to distant places. Parents and children who had been raised together were parted, their whereabouts unknown. Though the longing heart could not be exhausted, sighing and yet enduring, it was indeed so. This was the result of the Great Minister, the one who, holding the four seas in his palm, feared no one above and cared for no commoner below, who committed capital punishment and exile at his will, sparing neither the world nor people. It appears that there is no doubt that the sins of fathers and ancestors are repaid to their descendants.

text: かくて年月を過させ給ふ程に、女院御心地例ならず渡らせ給ひしかば、中尊の御手の五色の絲を引へつゝ、「南無西方極樂世界教主彌陀如來必ず引攝し給へ。」とて御念佛有しかば、大納言佐局阿波内侍左右に候て、今を限りの悲しさに聲を惜まず泣き叫ぶ。御念佛の聲やうやうよわらせましましければ西に紫雲靉靆き、異香室にみち、音樂空に聞ゆ。限ある事なれば、建久二年きさらぎの中旬に一期遂に終らせ給ひぬ。きさいの宮の御位より片時も離れまゐらせずして候はれ給しかば、御臨終の御時、別路に迷ひしも遣方なくぞおぼえける。此女房達は、昔の草のゆかりも枯果て、よる方もなき身なれども、折々の御佛事營み給ふぞ哀なる。終に彼人々は、龍女が正覺の跡をおひ、韋提希夫人の如に、皆往生の素懷を遂けるとぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: Thus, as time passed and the lady-in-waiting's health deteriorated beyond the norm, she took to drawing upon the five-colored silk threads of the Great Consecrated One, chanting, 'Namu Amida Nyorai, be sure to draw me into your embrace.' As she prayed with a voice growing increasingly weak, the Great Minister Sa's chambermaid and Awano no Naishi stood on either side of her, weeping and crying out without sparing their voices in their grief at this final sorrow. As her prayer grew faint, purple clouds gathered in the west, filling the room with a strange fragrance, and music was heard in the sky. Since all things are limited, in the middle of the second month of the second year of Kenkyū, her life finally came to an end. She never left the side of the Prince Kisa's palace for even a moment, and at the time of her death, she was said to have become lost on a separate path, with no one to guide her. These ladies-in-waiting, though their ties to the past had withered and they were now without even a home to call their own, found it deeply sorrowful to see her constantly perform Buddhist rites. Ultimately, it is said that those people followed in the footsteps of the Dragon Girl attaining perfect enlightenment, and like Lady Vaitāli, all accomplished their original aspiration for rebirth.
